title: Refusals on the hosted card
summary: The hosted card's four refusals in the catalog's words (DL8, B13), drawn the DL6 way: a full license (deviceLimit.title and heading, Replace a device), every license full (signin.choice.title with selectable rows tagged 'No free devices', signin.choice.allFull), a license sent to another email (activate.otherEmail.*, Use another account), and no key entries left (signin.key.noEntries, Sign in instead).
compare: Every refusal is a neutral callout on the sunken surface with a glyph, a strong first line and one sentence; no amber, no danger, no warning pill (B8, auth-08/09/10).
The fix is always the one primary (ink, block); there is never a disabled primary or a dead end: a second, quiet way out where one exists.
Key entries used up names when entries come back and turns the primary into Sign in instead; the key on-ramp header has no request verb (frame 4).
Amber is kept only for 'unsynced changes' on sign-out (not on this board).
Each frame keeps the product header strip; in a landscape window the same bodies sit in the form pane beside the passport.

Every string comes from packages/brand/kit-copy (deviceLimit.title/heading/lede, signin.choice.title/allFull, signin.choice.tag.full 'No free devices', signin.choice.keyInstead, activate.otherEmail.*, signin.none.otherAccount, signin.key.noEntries); none is invented on the board (M11).

All full: the licenses are a real radio group (the first, ranked, selected in the hosted card's core violet, B17) so Replace a device acts on the chosen one, and 'Use a license key instead' is the way out (M12).
Each frame has one ink primary and at most one quiet secondary; no amber, no disabled primary.
